doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Head arrangements versus written charts in the James Brown band
summary: Songs like Pass the Peas were built from spoken head arrangements; Down and Out in New York City had to be written out.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. I didn’t know how to do that, you know. But now “Pass the Peas” was a James Brown composition. I didn’t have anything to do with it except playing a solo on it. Because now James Brown — he would totally tell the band what to play, you know, and anything they didn’t understand I would translate it to them from James Brown you know. But James Brown said, “Have the trumpets play this” and “have the saxophones play this” and that you know. And so we learned James Brown’s music with the James Brown band by doing too. You know we’d say play this — and they finally understood what I was talking about and I understood what they were talking about and so that’s how we were successful with “Give Me Some Mo’”, “Pass the Peas” and even “Gonna Have a Funky Good time.” That was just talking, talking, talking it up and Jabo would play a shuffle. They’d say, “Jabo play a shuffle.” He would play a shuffle and the bass player would play [scats] and I had to figure out what [scats] what that was you know. And then I would translate it to the bass player. “Play this.” You know? And Fred Thomas would play [scats] and you put it all together and it would become a song you know. The guitar player would play, I didn’t know what the rhythm was — I still haven’t ever written [scats] I haven’t written that out, but if you just tell the guitar to play [scats] — do because we call those head arrangements. And so those head arrangements became big hits you know.

But then a tune like “Down and Out in New York City” those had to be written out by me from what James Brown told me. James Brown would say, “Have the horns do this, he wants the flutes to do this, you know, ridiculous things you know. But I would make it work you know.
